analysis: The PR changes only docs/developer/test.md, adding one paragraph at head lines 923-935 in the Flint native validation section. The paragraph documents two opt-in live test suites, FlintOpenRouterLiveTests and FlintRelayLogprobsLiveTests, gated by DARKBLOOM_FLINT_OPENROUTER_LIVE=1 and the existing Flint environment variables, with an optional DARKBLOOM_FLINT_RELAY_RECEIPTS file. No runtime, protocol, crypto or build code is changed, and the documentation grants no new authorization. I checked it against the threat model. It relates to TB-007, T-008, T-041 and A-001. The tests run over loopback with paged attention, and the relay logprobs test sends sealed requests to the production handler, so it exercises the encrypted path rather than bypassing it. The docs elsewhere already require synthetic or public prompts and say tokens, prompts and completions must not go to telemetry. The optional receipts file is the only new place output could be written. It may hold completion or logprob content, but the same section says the file must be owned and synthetic, and the tests use fixed inputs. I saw no weakening of the T-041 prefix-cache posture. The paged live path is separate from the cache controls, and existing instructions still require a fresh ephemeral cache root. The referenced test sources (FlintOpenRouterLiveTests.swift and FlintRelayLogprobsLiveTests.swift) were not supplied. Whether the tests actually keep to the stated bounds, such as synthetic data, a task-owned receipts path and no persistent cache keys, is therefore unverified. This is a note on coverage, not a finding. No regression found.
